chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who experiences janabah (major ritual impurity) during Ramadan, then sleeps before performing ghusl (ritual bath). He said: 'He completes his fast and makes up that day, unless he awakens before the rise of Fajr (dawn). If he waits for water to be heated or drawn, and Fajr rises, then he does not make up that day.'

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: Major ritual impurity requiring full body wash
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: The month of fasting in the Islamic calendar
key_terms.يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ: He completes his fast (for that day)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting if one sleeps in janabah until Fajr in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar clarifies that ritual impurity (janabah) itself does not invalidate the fast, provided one performs ghusl before dawn; the requirement to make up the day (qada) applies only if one sleeps past Fajr without a valid excuse. The exception for waiting for water to be heated or drawn highlights the Shia principle of removing hardship (raf' al-haraj), acknowledging that practical delays in accessing water do not constitute negligence. This distinction underscores the juristic focus on the intention and effort to purify oneself before the prayer time begins.
